evidence.snippet: - `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES`: a JSON array of `{ name, repo, base, head, file, rule?, alternativeRules?, fix?, lines? }`, each a `needs-execution` miss in a clone on the machine. `fix` names the commit that fixed it; `lines` is the first and last line of the defect at the head. A sighting under `rule` or any of `alternativeRules` can find the miss. A miss may leave out `rule` only when it has `lines`, and then a sighting under any rule at those lines finds it; `alternativeRules` needs a `rule`. Each rule must be one some lens of the base's `full` tier declares for the file, in either mode, so one misses file serves both and a misspelt alternative exits 2. In `lens` mode one of them must be `trust-boundary`'s. A miss is scored on the reviewing lenses' own sightings at the head, `trust-boundary`'s in `lens` mode and every lens check's in `whole`, read from the review's store level by level, because a finding merged with another lens's, or with another level's, keeps only its speaker's lines and words. An ID excludes lines, so quick and careful can sight one ID at different lines, and the verifier can refute one and uphold the other. A sighting answers the miss when the verdict holds the claim of its check, ID and level unrefuted, it sits at the file under one of the miss's rules, or any rule when it names none, and it overlaps those lines. The claim may sit in any of the verdict's groups, so a refuted one scores the miss as not found. A dismissed claim counts by its own verification, since the measurement asks whether the lens sighted the defect and the verifier let it stand, and a dismissal is a person's later call that a fresh store cannot hold. A sighting the verdict holds no claim for, a reviewing lens's claim with no sighting, or a claim the verdict holds twice, leaves that miss with no score, as a failed review does. The score follows the verdict: an unrefuted claim counts whether or not its probe was sound, and the results file is what lets a reader check. Without `lines`, they come from git's diff  [cut at 2 KiB]
- `needs-execution`: it was found by running code, not by reading it. It joins [verifier evals](#verifier-evals) and the tool manifest's list, not the lens golden corpus.
